subject: Request: temporary client-side retry toggle for low-latency demos
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@democorp.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask before tomorrow's low-latency demo

Hi Tessa / Marissa,

We have the customer-facing demo with our internal execs tomorrow at 10:30 PT and noticed intermittent retries from the client during the last dry run. Those retries double up token usage and occasionally surface duplicate outputs during the live walkthrough — it's become a distraction.

Can Redwood temporarily disable the automatic client-side retry behavior for our tenant for the 10:00–11:00 PT window tomorrow? If shutting retries off entirely isn't safe, could we get a short-lived exemption or a config that skips retries on 5xx/timeout for demo traffic?

We understand this isn’t ideal for production, just need a controlled mitigation for one scheduled demo. Any quickpath you can offer would be amazing.

Attached: demo-recording.mp4 (short clip showing duplicates).

Thanks,
Alice
Customer Success Manager
DemoCorp
[Attachment: demo-recording.mp4 (video)]

From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: logan_wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Alice Nguyen <alice@democorp.com>
Date: Thu, 2 May 2029 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Quick ask before tomorrow's low-latency demo

Hi all,

Looping in runtime + SDK to triage. Short context: DemoCorp is asking for a temporary way to avoid client-side retries during a scheduled demo window because retries are causing duplicate outputs and higher token billing during demos.

Ask: Is there a safe, fast path to either (A) flip a tenant-scoped flag to disable client retry logic for this tenant for a defined time window, or (B) provide an SDK-level feature flag that our sales engs can enable locally for the demo?

Requirements from Sales:
- Quick turn (ideally < 8 hours) for tomorrow's 10:30 PT slot (they're aware this is tight).
- Reversible: we should be able to re-enable retries instantly after the window.
- Limited blast radius: change only affects DemoCorp traffic, not global behavior.

Attachments: I pulled a repro.zip that contains the client trace from their dry run.

Can you triage feasibility + minimum-risk approach? If this needs a runtime-side change (Dev), what are the rollout and rollback steps? If SDK toggle (Logan), how fast could you ship a small patch or a locally patched binary we can use?

Thanks — Tessa
Tessa Morgan | Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: demo-repro.zip (logs + trace)]

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Alice Nguyen <alice@democorp.com>
Date: Thu, 2 May 2029 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Quick ask before tomorrow's low-latency demo

Thanks Tessa — reviewed the repro. Quick technical summary: the client retries are happening because the SDK uses an exponential backoff on transient 5xx / connection timeouts and also replays the final prompt chunk on reconnect. For demo workflows that need strict single-invoke semantics, we can do one of two things:

Option 1 (fast, SDK-only): Add an environment/switch flag (e.g., REDWOOD_SDK_SKIP_RETRY=true) that bypasses retry logic entirely in the client for the process. We can build a small patched wheel/binary today and ship an instrumented SDK tarball that Sales can use for tomorrow. Minimal runtime changes, zero tenant config, easy rollback (just stop using the patched SDK). Risk: if network hiccups occur, the demo could show a failed response rather than a delayed success.

Option 2 (safer, runtime/light-change): Add a tenant-scoped runtime header that instructs the serving runtime to accept idempotency tokens from the client and not requeue requests. This requires a small runtime change + a canary deploy to ensure no side-effects for multi-tenant caching/batching. Estimated work: 1–2 days dev + 1 day for safe canary and rollback plan.

I can produce the SDK patched build today. I've sketched a minimal design doc — attaching: sdk-retry-flag-proposal.md.

Proposed immediate action: ship SDK patch for tomorrow's demo; follow up with runtime tenant-flag work to provide a tenant-scoped, auditable opt-out for retries.

— Logan
Logan Wright | Senior SDK Engineer, Redwood
[Attachment: sdk-retry-flag-proposal.md]

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, logan_wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 May 2029 13:55:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Quick ask before tomorrow's low-latency demo

Appreciate the clear options. Operational notes from runtime side:

- Option 1 (SDK patch) is fine as a stopgap and is the lowest risk to cluster stability. Recommend sales run the patched SDK from an isolated host so we can segregate metrics. No runtime deployment required.

- Option 2 (tenant opt-out header) touches queuing/batching/kv-cache semantics. If we accept requests with "skip-retry" semantics, we must ensure downstream deduplication / idempotency token handling doesn't break multi-tenant cache invariants. That requires a small kernel-safe check and a rollout: feature flag -> canary (1% traffic) -> monitor token replay metrics and latency.

Estimated timeline for Option 2: 48–72 hours (dev+canary+monitoring). For the demo tomorrow, Option 1 is the path of least resistance.

I'll prepare a runtime-config proposal that documents the safe rollout and monitoring hooks. See attached. I can also provision a temporary per-tenant ACL in the routing layer to ensure only DemoCorp traffic is affected if we do the runtime route.

— Dev
Dev Patel | Platform Runtime Engineer
[Attachment: runtime-config-proposal.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@democorp.com>
Cc: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, logan_wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 May 2029 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Quick ask before tomorrow's low-latency demo — plan and confirmation

Hi Alice — quick update and confirmed plan: 

1) For tomorrow's demo we will use a patched SDK build that disables client-side retries. Logan will provide the patched binary and installation notes by EOD today. Please use the provided binary only for the demo host; keep your normal integration untouched.

2) Dev will follow up to scope a tenant-level runtime opt-out (longer-term, ~48–72 hours) so you have a supported mechanism for future demos. That will include monitoring and an audit trail.

3) I'll schedule a 30-minute sync post-demo to validate results and discuss whether we want the runtime opt-out as part of the DC-47891 deal commitments.

Thanks to the engineering team for the quick turn. Logan — send the SDK tarball + checksum. Dev — please share the canary checklist when ready.

Best,
Marissa Cole | Sales Engineering Manager, Redwood
